explanation: Some workers, called repletes, hang from the ceilings of underground chambers with bellies swollen like grapes. Nestmates feed from them, and Aboriginal Australians dig them up as a sweet treat.

claims.text: Honeypot ants store liquid food in the swollen abdomens of special workers called repletes.
Honeypot ants do not store food in wax honeycombs, mud cells or hollowed-out seeds.
Repletes hang from the ceilings of underground nest chambers, their abdomens swollen with stored food.
Other ants in the nest feed on food regurgitated by repletes.
Aboriginal Australians dig up honeypot ants and eat them as a sweet food.
